detectors.bf16_fixed: any coordinate differs by more than one bfloat16 spacing of the reference value
detectors.cosine_calibrated: largest per-row 1 - cosine above the largest seen on the floor's nulls
detectors.fp32_hash: SHA-256 of the float32 bytes differs
detectors.max_abs_calibrated: largest absolute coordinate difference above the largest seen on the floor's nulls

results.draw_seeds: SHA-256 of the JSON ['floor-power', pool, draw]; first 8 bytes, big-endian, seed np.random.default_rng

faults.diffuse: Gaussian noise of c times the pool's null scale on every coordinate, renormalized
faults.replace: k fault documents take the vector of other documents of the same run
faults.size: median over draws of the median 1 - cosine of the modified rows to the held-out null
faults.sparse: a share of the coordinates multiplied by (1 + scale) in every row, renormalized
faults.substitute: words of one document replaced by random corpus words, embedded in the same session
faults.truncate: one document keeps the first (1 - cut) of its words, embedded in the same session

limits: one corpus (SciFact, 5,183 documents) and one model (e5-small-v2)
the varying pool is synthetic: real rebuilds here gave one SEMQ state per device
the draws resample one fixed pool; the intervals describe that pool, not the rebuilds of another pipeline
the bounds 2/(N+1) for within and 3/(N+1) for per-row assume the nulls and the candidate are exchangeable

synthetic.description: each null is an accelerator null of the real pool, taken in turn, plus independent Gaussian noise on every coordinate of its rows and fault vectors, renormalized; it models a rebuild whose noise varies from run to run

results.procedure: each draw permutes the pool, holds out the first null, and measures Floor.measure(per_row=True) from the next N; the held-out null is judged for false alarms; each fault is applied to the held-out null and judged at the detection N. Calibrated float checks use the same N nulls
results.question: How often does the floor reject an unchanged rebuild, and how often does it catch a real fault, next to float checks on the same vectors?
